evidence: The lower location is a green triangle and dominates current attention and access; its information is the most available now and after one or two steps.
The right location is effectively a blue square with modest availability if selected.
The left location is a yellow circle with poor availability.
The upper location is highly uncertain in both color and shape (no single color or shape identified) and is minimally available.

Predicted responses to attention commands are strongly self-consistent: each command mostly maintains or returns selection to its current focus, so the system has limited ability to reallocate attention away from the dominant lower item.
The lower location is a yellow circle and is the clear focus with the highest availability.
The left is a blue triangle
the right is a red square
Command predictions in B largely steer selection toward the right location for many commands, so control over where attention moves is constrained and not broadly flexible.
